 In this role, you will bring deep expertise across social platforms, audience behavior, content strategy, and cultural intelligence to uncover opportunities for brands to show up in meaningful and authentic ways. You understand that effective social strategy lives at the intersection of consumer insights, brand values, platform dynamics, and culture. By connecting these elements, you will help brands create content ecosystems that resonate with audiences, inspire engagement, and strengthen long-term brand affinity.  
 As a core member of the team, you will partner closely with Creative, Insights, Analytics, Media, and Client Services to translate audience needs, emerging trends, and social behaviors into actionable strategic recommendations. You are equal parts strategist, storyteller, and trusted advisor, with a passion for helping brands navigate the evolving social landscape and identify the conversations, communities, and cultural moments that matter most.  
 The ideal candidate brings a strong point of view on how social can drive brand growth through purposeful content, community engagement, creator and influencer ecosystems, and culturally relevant storytelling. They are energized by turning insights into strategic frameworks that help brands build deeper connections with people, earn attention in crowded feeds, and create lasting relevance beyond individual campaigns.

- Executive Client Leadership & Presentation:  Act as the primary strategic client lead, driving client relationship growth and presenting high-impact decks directly to Director, VP, and executive-level client stakeholders.

Define how brands can authentically participate in conversations, communities, and moments that matter, establishing a clear role for social in driving audience engagement and brand growth.  
- Audience & Content Ecosystem Mapping:  Identify audience motivations, behaviors, and unmet needs to develop platform-specific content strategies. Define audience segments, content pillars, engagement approaches, and creator opportunities that build relevance and foster ongoing community participation  
- Insight & Trend Translation:  Synthesize social listening, consumer research, performance data, and emerging cultural trends to uncover actionable opportunities for brands. Translate insights into strategic recommendations that strengthen audience connection, cultural resonance, and market differentiation.  
- Strategic Narrative & Storytelling:  Distill raw data, research, and channel mechanics into executive-ready narratives and actionable business recommendations.   
- Measurement & Optimization:  Establish social KPIs and measurement frameworks that evaluate channel performance and quantify social's contribution to broader marketing and business outcome

 You will work on a Scrum team within a SAFe Agile framework. Success in this role requires analytical and technical expertise, sound judgment, clear communication, collaboration, business insight, an inclusive mindset and a commitment to continuous learning.

 In this role, you will turn complex investment accounting needs into clear requirements and coordinated technology delivery.

 • Participate in SAFe Agile ceremonies - PI Planning, backlog replenishment, standups, sprint reviews and retrospectives - and contribute to release planning.  
 • Support conversion and upgrade projects, new data feed onboarding and multi-platform integration efforts.  
 • Use enterprise-approved AI tools, including Microsoft Copilot, Atlassian Rovo and Claude Code, to accelerate requirements analysis, documentation, data investigation, test preparation and delivery while applying sound judgment, validation and responsible-use practices.  
 • Set and manage delivery dates that meet client requirements, partnering with clients, business stakeholders and technology teams throughout the project lifecycle.  
 • Look for opportunities to improve our analysis practices, documentation standards and tooling - and to coach others as you do.  
 What you will bring  
 • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering or a related field (or equivalent experience).  
 • 7+ years of business or systems analysis experience delivering technology change, ideally in financial services, with an understanding of financial concepts, metrics and business outcomes.

 • Experience with Agile development practices and supporting tools such as JIRA and Confluence.

workday:R-125158.description:
Job Classification:
Investment Management - Investments 
 A GLOBAL FIRM WITH A CURIOSITY-DRIVEN CULTURE 
 As the global asset management business of Prudential, we’re solving financial challenges for millions of people around the world. To do that we need top talent, which we attract by fostering a truly collaborative culture in which everyone is encouraged to keep asking . We seek clarity and insight at all stages, from delving into individual security characteristics to understanding our clients’ investment goals at the broadest level.
 If you’re not afraid to think differently and challenge the status quo, come and be a part of a dedicated team at one of the world’s leading global asset managers!
 What you will do 
 PGIM’s Strategic Capital Group (SCG) is responsible for providing institutional clients with asset-liability management, portfolio strategy, and asset allocation solutions harnessing PGIM’s multi-asset expertise across public and private credit. SCG oversees liability-aware portfolio construction and strategic asset design on behalf of its clients, while also partnering with other teams including PGIM Credit and PGIM Real Estate to deliver best-in-class private origination, credit underwriting, investment research, and risk management capabilities across a full range of asset classes. SCG is the investment manager for Prismic, a reinsurance platform launched by Prudential together with other strategic investors.
 This position is within the Portfolio Analytics team of SCG and will assume key responsibilities in the growth of our state-of-the-art quant platform for dynamic portfolio optimization based on rigorous asset-liability simulation and economic scenario generation. You will focus, in particular, on modeling the dynamics of diverse asset classes as well as underlying economic risk factors, which will feed into real portfolio construction projects, both for live deals and in-force business, not just post-allocation diagnostics.
 You will be based in our Newark, NJ office and will follow a hybrid schedule (3 days in-office).
 What you can expect 
- Build stochastic models to enhance and extend our proprietary real-world economic scenario generator
- Contribute to macro-factor and asset-level models that set key parameters within the scenario generator
- Develop advanced techniques to analyze emerging asset classes with sparse historical data
- Develop methodology and tools for attributing changes in asset-liability metrics to underlying risk factors
- Investigate and apply the latest quantitative and AI-based methods to concrete investment-strategy problems
- Work with teams across PGIM to properly model investment strategies across a range of public, private, and structured asset classes for use within our asset-liability simulations
 What you will bring 
- Economics or Finance Ph.D., advanced degree from a quantitative finance program, or comparable academic experience within a quantitative discipline
- Solid programming background, including Python (pandas, numpy, scipy) and exposure to modern transformer technology and foundation models
- Reliable knowledge of core quant finance topics: probability theory, statistics, stochastic models, options theory, yield curve construction, fixed income analytics, CAPM, etc.—both at the technical level but also conceptually, in terms of basic financial intuitions accessible to non-quants
 What will set you apart 
- Familiarity with structured products, private credit, real estate debt, and private equity, as well as previous exposure to insurance liabilities and asset-liability management concepts
- Knowledge about the theoretical foundations of quant finance and about macroeconomic frameworks
- Creativity, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to break down quantitative ideas for non-quant audiences
 *PGIM welcomes all applicants, even if you don't meet every requirement. If your skills align with the role, we encourage you to apply. 
 Not

 At PGIM, You Can!  
 What you will do 
 The Senior Analyst will provide day-to-day operational support for PGIM Credit’s Securities Lending business. This role serves as a key control point across the loan lifecycle, supporting loan execution, returns, restructures, recalls, settlements management, and related issue resolution.
 In this role, you will partner closely with Securities Lending traders, broker-dealers, custodian banks, technology partners, and internal Operations teams to ensure timely, accurate, and well-controlled processing across cash-collateralized lending activity, including Corporate Bonds and U.S. Treasury securities. The successful candidate will bring strong operations knowledge, attention to detail, sound judgment, and a proactive approach to risk reduction, escalation, and process improvement.
 This position is based in our office in Newark, NJ and will follow a hybrid schedule. Our organization follows a hybrid work structure ( 3 days in office) where employees can work remotely and/ from the office, as needed, based on demands of specific tasks or personal work preferences. Working from the office is encouraged when working on tasks that require a high degree of collaboration.
 What you can expect 
- Monitor and support the daily settlement of securities lending loans, returns, recalls, restructures, and sale-related activity, ensuring timely resolution of exceptions and breaks.
- Act as a primary operational point of contact for Securities Lending traders, broker-dealers, custodians, and internal Operations partners across the loan lifecycle.
- Manage operational issues through resolution, coordinating across impacted teams and communicating status, risks, and required actions clearly and timely.
- Identify, escalate, and mitigate risks related to settlement fails, buy-ins, loan recalls, corporate actions, restructures, overdrafts, and client or portfolio impact.
- Support cash-collateralized lending activity for fixed income products, including Corporate Bonds and U.S. Treasury securities, in accordance with established controls and procedures.
- Analyze activity, trends, breaks, and key operating metrics to support management reporting, risk monitoring, and continuous improvement.
- Partner with technology and operations teams to identify automation opportunities, reduce manual risk, improve scalability, and enhance the overall control environment.
- Maintain strong internal and external relationships to support service levels, timely escalation, and effective issue resolution across the Securities Lending platform.
- Stay informed on industry initiatives, market structure changes, settlement practices, and regulatory developments that may affect securities lending operations.

Job Classification:
Investment Management - Investments 
 What you will do 
 As an Associate on the North American Distribution team, you’ll serve as a key partner to senior sales professionals, supporting their efforts to develop new relationships, deepen existing ones, and raise capital across PGIM’s investment platform. The role offers high visibility internally, regular interaction with clients, consultants, and PGIM investment professionals, and meaningful opportunities for professional growth and development.
 What you can expect 
- Support senior sales professionals in covering their territories and client segments—fostering relationships, advancing opportunities, and managing day-to-day business activities
- Prepare for and attend prospect and client meetings, including coordinating logistics, assisting in the production of meeting books and pitchbooks, and drafting meeting notes and follow-ups
- Partner with sales and investment teams to proactively identify prospects and prepare analyses that position PGIM strategies effectively
- Respond to client, prospect, and consultant inquiries, including data requests, strategy materials, and search-related information
- Coordinate responses to RFPs, RFIs, and due diligence questionnaires (DDQs) alongside the RFP, product, marketing, and compliance teams
- Conduct research and competitive analysis on institutional investors, consultants, peer managers, asset allocation trends, and industry developments
- Maintain accurate CRM (Salesforce) data—logging call notes, updating opportunities, and contributing to pipeline tracking, business metrics, and reporting
- Leverage core sales and research tools, including Salesforce, eVestment, Seismic, With Intelligence, FinSearches, Preqin, and various other industry databases
- Coordinate across Portfolio Management, Product Specialists, Marketing, Consultant Relations, Client Management, Sales Enablement, Legal, and Compliance to deliver accurate, approved materials
- Contribute to broader team initiatives focused on business growth, process improvement, and strategic priorities
 What you will bring 
- 3-5  years of experience in asset management.
- Familiarity with institutional investor types, investment consultants, and the manager search process.
- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint, and the broader Microsoft Office Suite.
- Experience with Salesforce or other CRM platforms, and investment databases such as eVestment, Preqin, or With Intelligence.
- FINRA Series 7, FINRA Series 63, and NFA Series 3 (or willingness to obtain)
- Progress toward the CFA or CAIA designation
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Business, Data Analytics, Statistics, or related disciplines; all majors considered.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build relationships and present information clearly to clients, colleagues, and senior management.
- Proven ability to multitask, prioritize competing deadlines, and work well under pressure with strong follow-through.
 Note: Prudential is required by state specific laws to include the salary range for this role when hiring a resident in applicable locations. The salary range for this role is from $95,000 to $130,000. Specific pricing for the role may vary within the above range based on many factors including geographic location, candidate experience, and skills. Roles may also be eligible for additional compensation and/or benefits.
 About PGIM’s Institutional Client Group 
 PGIM’s Institutional Client Group North American Distribution team sits at the heart of how we connect the world’s largest institutional investors—public and corporate pension plans, Taft-Hartley plans, insurers, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, foundations, and the consultants who advise them—with PGIM’s investment capabilities across public and private markets. Working across consultant relations, client relationship management, sales

Humana's Corporate Strategy team is a small, high-performing group that works closely with senior leadership to establish the future course for the company. In Corporate Strategy, you will identify and analyze growth opportunities and work with business leaders to prioritize options and set the long-term strategy agenda. The team has frequent interactions with Humana’s CEO and regularly manages deliverables for Humana’s broader Executive Leadership Team and Board of Directors. Our team also undertakes internal consulting engagements across a wide range of topics. 
 The Corporate Strategy Lead plays a critical role in the successful delivery of projects, owning responsibility for one or more simultaneously and managing workstreams of junior colleagues. Leads are required to manage the scope of work, understand the needs of stakeholders within Corporate Strategy and elsewhere in Humana, and ensure high-quality results that bring out the best thinking of the team. Examples of project work include identifying and evaluating growth opportunities across our lines of business, developing market and competitive strategies, assessing partnership and acquisition opportunities, designing operating model / organizational improvements, and supporting pilots / innovation opportunities for various business leaders

- Lead strategic analyses and recommendations on high-priority enterprise initiatives.
- Facilitate discussions with business leaders to identify opportunities and address strategic challenges.
- Develop business cases to support investment decisions and growth initiatives.
- Translate strategic recommendations into actionable implementation plans.
- Mentor analysts and provide guidance on project execution and analytical approaches.
- Collaborate with Corporate Strategy colleagues, and contribute to a high-performing, inclusive, and supportive team environment
 Use your skills to make an impact

- Bachelor’s Degree
- 5+ years of consulting, strategy, or relevant corporate experience (i.e., strategic in nature vs. primarily operational)
- Analytical skills (ex: quantitative analysis and research, financial modeling)
- Conceptual skills (ex: translating ambiguous problem statements into structured frameworks, generating hypotheses independently and testing them, synthesizing complex information into digestible executive insights, managing cross-functional stakeholders)
   Preferred Qualifications 
- Graduate from a top-tier master’s program in business, health administration, or related field
- Meaningful experience in strategy consulting, corporate strategy, or investment banking / corporate development
- Relevant healthcare experience, especially in payer industry

The Program Lead, Enterprise Clinical Partnerships (ECP) Performance Management, is responsible for driving the success of Humana's portfolio of enterprise clinical partnerships through strategic oversight, performance management, operational governance, and cross-functional collaboration. This role serves as a key connector between internal business partners and external clinical vendors to ensure programs deliver measurable value for members, providers, and Humana.
The Program Lead will lead performance improvement initiatives, develop executive insights and recommendations, drive accountability across stakeholders, and enhance Humana's performance management capabilities through data-driven decision-making and operational excellence. This role will support a variety of clinical partnership types, with a preference for candidates who bring expertise in Behavioral Health, value-based care, and population health strategies. 
 The Enterprise Clinical Partnerships Performance Management team is responsible for evaluating, monitoring, and improving the performance of Humana's clinical partnership portfolio, including specialty care, Behavioral Health, and other population health-focused programs. The Program Lead works across Clinical Strategy, Behavioral Health, Market Operations, Analytics, Care Management, Product, Finance, Network, and Vendor Management teams to drive outcomes, optimize performance, and support enterprise objectives.
 This role combines strategic thinking, operational leadership, analytics, and stakeholder management to identify opportunities, solve complex business challenges, and advance Humana's clinical and value-based care strategy.
 In This Role You Will 
- Lead performance management activities across a portfolio of Enterprise Clinical Partnership programs, including Behavioral Health and other strategic clinical partnerships.
- Analyze clinical, operational, financial, enrollment, engagement, quality, access, and outcome metrics to identify opportunities and risks.
- Partner with internal Behavioral Health, Clinical Strategy, Care Management, and external vendor leaders to identify and execute performance improvement initiatives.
- Support the development and implementation of innovative care models that improve member outcomes and experience, particularly in Behavioral Health and complex population management.
- Identify trends, emerging risks, and market opportunities across the clinical partnership portfolio and recommend strategic actions.

- 7+ years of experience in healthcare operations, strategy, performance management, consulting, vendor management, program management or behavioral health

- Demonstrated success influencing internal and external stakeholders without direct authority
- Ability to balance strategic planning with operational execution in complex healthcare environments
 Role Desirables 
- Experience with Behavioral Health programs, Behavioral Health operations, Behavioral Health vendor management, or Behavioral Health strategy
- Experience with value-based care, population health, specialty care, or clinical vendor partnerships
- Experience managing external vendor performance and contractual accountability

- Experience leading performance improvement initiatives related to Behavioral Health, clinical outcomes, member experience, or operational transformation

Head of Treasury Capital Markets 
 Position Summary
 Do you want to be part of a collaborative Treasury team?  Do you have corporate Treasury experience, are detail oriented and possess good interpersonal skills to effectively interface between Treasury and Business and Investment teams?  Do you think big and grow, accelerate impact, and lead change?    If so, Guardian is seeking a Head of Treasury Capital Markets to lead Guardian’s treasury team to manage Guardian’s financial transactions. 
 You are
 A collaborative, self-starter who will work across the Enterprise to manage the complex financial transactions supporting Guardian’s capital management and growth strategies, including  the Funding Agreement Backed Notes business.  You are focused on driving Guardian’s strategic priorities of growth and capital management.  You are comfortable working with tight deadlines to initiate and complete financial transactions. 
 You have
 Required: 
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance or a related discipline 
- 10-15  years of experience 
- Strong analytical,  interpersonal and leadership skills 
- Knowledge of Treasury Management Systems, with experience with Kyriba a plus. 
 Preferred: 
- Experience with FHLB borrowing process and collateral posting requirements including Commercial & Residential Mortgage Loans 
- Knowledge of FHLB 1Link Systems a plus 
- The ability to accelerate impact and lead change 
 You will
- Manage Guardian borrowing programs, including external credit facilities, surplus notes, internal loans, and internal lines of credit.  Review debt agreements and monitor key financial  and operational requirements. 
- Lead the capital markets activities of Guardian’s Treasury team, which includes managing the FHLB program for borrowing, repayments, interest, stock requirements, optimizing collateral posted to the FHLB, and all required reporting to internal parties, FHLB, and DFS. 
- Collaborate with Investments executives to establish and fund warehouses for FABN program (including FHLB or other funding mechanisms), manage issuances, payments and maturities 
- Strategically manage Guardian’s debt activity to provide visibility into program utilization and upcoming interest payments, renewals and maturities.   Manage financial reporting aspects of these programs. 
- Assist Treasury leadership with capital structure, financing and liquidity analysis. 
- Collaborate with the Investments and Risk senior leaders to support capital management and forecasting, scenario analysis and stress-testing activities. 
- Be the subject matter expert for senior leaders across Guardian on these programs. 
 Reporting Relationships
 As our Head of Treasury Capital Markets, you will report to Guardian’s Assistant Treasurer, who reports to the Treasurer .
 Location
 The primary location for this position is New York City (Hudson Yards).  Applicants may also work from Guardian’s Holmdel NJ, Bethlehem PA or Pittsfield MA locations. 
 Travel
 Very limited travel is required for this position.
 Salary Range: 
$135,070.00 - $221,897.50 
 The salary range reflected above is a good faith estimate of base pay for the primary location of the position. The salary for this position ultimately will be determined based on the education, experience, knowledge, and abilities of the successful candidate. In addition to salary, this role may also be eligible for annual, sales, or other incentive compensation.
 Our Promise 
 At Guardian, you’ll have the support and flexibility to achieve your professional and personal goals.  Through skill-building, leadership development and philanthropic opportunities, we provide opportunities to build communities and grow your career, surrounded by diverse colleagues with high ethical standards.

Enterprise Risk Management – Analyst 
 ORIX Enterprise Risk Management is seeking an Analyst to be based in either of ORIX Corporation USA’s New York or Dallas offices. The investment professional will be an integral part of the team, responsible for supporting ERM’s stress testing program as well as a wide variety of enterprise-wide risk activities.
 The ORIX Enterprise Risk Management team is focused on identifying, monitoring, evaluating and managing financial and non-financial risks across the firm. The mission of the Enterprise Risk Management function is to provide risk information, guidance, tools, and standards, and to drive a culture of risk awareness to support appropriate and timely risk related decisions within the organization. ORIX Corporation USA (“ORIX USA”) and our family of companies offer investment capital and asset management services to portfolio companies in the corporate, real estate, and municipal finance sectors.
 Essential Duties & Responsibilities 
- Support ORIX USA’s enterprise-wide stress testing framework and governance.
- Become an expert in ORIX USA’s portfolio composition, position data and diverse set of industries.
- Coordinate with functional areas (credit risk, accounting, treasury, etc.) to fully understand the portfolio, loss drivers and variances over time.
- Collaborate with the credit teams within ORIX USA’s business groups to ensure the appropriate business assumptions are utilized in the stress testing methodology.
- Coordinate with accounting on CECL reserve analytics modeling.
- Proactively manage non-financial risk (NFR) activities, including monitoring key risk indicators (KRIs), risk & control self assessments (RCSAs) and NFR escalations.
- Produce reports that identify sustainability risk for both balance sheet and mandate assets 
- Monitor compliance with ORIX USA’s Risk Appetite Statement and stress testing requirements.
- Produce ad-hoc documentation and presentations to effectively communicate key information.
- Develop or implement additional risk-assessment models and methodologies.
- Work closely with the ERM team at the parent company, ORIX Corporation, and provide transparency into monitoring and governance processes.
 Contacts 
 This role involves working with a variety of business groups and risk professionals across the organization, including ORIX USA’s parent company, ORIX Corporation, based in Tokyo, Japan. The position offers opportunities to gain exposure to all aspects of enterprise risk management.
 Education, Skills & Experience 
 The environment at ORIX USA is both collegial and entrepreneurial. Teamwork is essential to the firm’s success. At the same time, creativity and new ideas are encouraged. The position involves substantial responsibility; you are expected to help us manage the risk analytics of our business.
 Ideal candidates will possess the following: 
- Bachelor’s degree from an accredited four-year university in finance, economics, or related field
- Master’s degree in a relevant field preferred (Finance, Business, ERM, etc.)
- Professional qualifications in risk management or finance

- Strong work ethic, motivated and positive attitude with ability to work independently

Summary: 
 Neuberger Wealth is seeking a highly motivated and results-driven individual to lead initiatives focused on process improvement and operational excellence. This individual will play a critical role in enhancing the efficiency, scalability, and effectiveness of the Neuberger Wealth business by evaluating current processes, identifying opportunities for improvement, and driving implementation efforts. The role requires a blend of strategic thinking, operational expertise, and change management capabilities.
 As a member of the Wealth Platforms & Experience organization, the role of the Analyst will be responsible for the ownership and execution of several strategic programs and analyses related to Private Wealth’s Client Service Journey. 
The candidate will be a detail oriented strategic thinker with a passion for solving complex problems, dealing with ambiguity, organizational design, and who possesses an unrelenting customer obsession and a strong desire to make their mark on the organization.

- Journey Definition 
- Own and enhance all aspects of the Client Service journey across the Wealth business (transacting, trading, maintenance, inquiry, self-service)
- Create and maintain journey maps, process flows, SOPs, and playbooks and training materials across the end-to-end client onboarding journey
- Identify friction points and recommend enhancements that reduce handoffs, processing times, and error rates

- Establish and track SLAs and KPIs

- Partner with Enterprise Data Governance to define and maintain client and account data dictionaries and validation rules. Ensure consistency across the ecosystem and all client and advisor touchpoints
- Inventory and rationalize Client Service forms and documentation requirements with the goal of simplification of workflows
- Maintain an inventory and prioritization of known tech debt / enhancements

- Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, Operations Management, Engineering, or a related field
- 5+ years of experience in Wealth Management / Private Banking. Direct experience with client service, product ownership, or business analysis a plus
- Strong knowledge of process mapping, workflow analysis, and operational efficiency tools
- Proficiency in automation technologies and familiarity with digital transformation initiatives
- Experience in change management principles and techniques
- Candidate must be a self-starter with the ability to operate independently and make decisions
- Ability to build relationships and partner across a complex organization
- Ability to multi-task and manage multiple simultaneous projects
- Ability to influence seniors and stakeholders outside of your span of control
- Excellent time management, follow-through, and project delivery skills
- Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, able to simplify complexity
- Exceptional analytical skills
- Strategic thinker
- Strong attention to detail
- Highly organized
- Owner of outcomes
- Team player

Position Overview 
At PNC, our people are our greatest differentiator and competitive advantage in the markets we serve. We are all united in delivering the best experience for our customers. We work together each day to foster an inclusive workplace culture where all of our employees feel respected, valued and have an opportunity to contribute to the company’s success. As a Field Exam Analyst within PNC's Business Credit organization, you will be based in one of the following locations: Los Angeles, CA; Pasadena, CA; Atlanta, GA; Chicago, IL; Dallas, TX, New York, NY; Philadelphia, PA; or Pittsburgh, PA.
As a Field Exam Analyst, you will evaluate borrower's financial records, collateral and operational processes to help assess risk. You will prepare reports of findings and provide recommendations that support sound credit decisions. This position requires regular time in the field, including on-site client examinations, and will involve overnight travel on a recurring basis. 
Preferred skills/experience include, but are not limited to the following: 
• A minimum of 1+ years of Asset Based Lending (ABL) Field Exam experience
• Familiarity with corporate accounting through coursework and/or job experience
• Advanced Excel skills 
PNC is an in-office company that fosters a supportive culture where employees can thrive and achieve balance. We encourage candidates to connect with their recruiter and hiring manager to understand workplace expectations and ensure the role aligns with their goals.  
PNC will not provide sponsorship for employment visas or participate in STEM OPT for this position. 
 Job Description 
- Leads less complex Field Examinations on existing and prospective borrowers and assists on Field Examinations led by other examiners. Examinations can take place fully onsite at Borrower locations or in a hybrid on-site/remote environment.
- Performs independent analysis on existing Borrower's collateral records and financial reports to determine / assess collateral values that secure loans and to identify and highlight areas of collateral weakness or deterioration.    Evaluates accounting system controls, data integrity, managerial control oversight and borrowers accounting personnel.
